evidence.note: claim: merge.require_gates is reported dead because merge_force.mode_of read it via getattr(sect,'require_gates','warn'), which the name-based ratchet regex (\\.merge\\.require_gates) cannot see even though MergeConfig is registered in Config (ddflow/config/_core.py:167). mechanism: dead_knobs() enumerates Config.load().explain() then _read_in_any regex-scans sources for the literal .merge.require_gates. probe: python -c 'from tests.test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs import dead_knobs; print(dead_knobs(["merge.require_gates"]))' -> ['merge.require_gates'] on unfixed main; after reading cfg.merge.require_gates -> []. VERDICT CONFIRMED.

change follows the config consumption contract: mode_of reads the declared knob via cfg.merge.require_gates (the ratchet's canonical read form), not a bare policy literal or an invisible getattr. No new literal policy decision introduced.
wired merge.require_gates read in mode_of to cfg.merge.require_gates; added regression tests (dead_knobs(["merge.require_gates"])==[] and knob-refuse agent-force refusal).

chunk_findings.detail: The change replaces the guarded read with `return cfg.merge.require_gates or "warn"`, but the stated bug context says the `Merge` section is not registered in `Config`, and this diff does not register it. On a default `Config` with no `merge` section, `mode_of(cfg)` now evaluates `cfg.merge` and raises `AttributeError` instead of returning `"warn"` as the previous `getattr(cfg, "merge", None)` did. For example, invoking a merge that calls `assess`/`mode_of` against an unconfigured repo will crash before any `warn` handling, while the new test only passes because it first runs `config merge.require_gates refuse`, which creates the missing section.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/merge_force.py:44 (mode_of)

chunk_findings.detail: The new `return cfg.merge.require_gates or "warn"` dereferences `cfg.merge` unconditionally. The bug context says the `Merge` section is not registered in `Config`, so a normal/default config has no usable `cfg.merge`; the previous code handled that with `getattr(cfg, "merge", None)` and fell back to `"warn"`. Given input `ddflow merge` with a default config lacking `[merge]`, `assess` calls `mode_of(cfg)` and now raises `AttributeError` (`'Config' object has no attribute 'merge'` or `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'require_gates'`) instead of returning `"warn"`, breaking the default merge path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/merge_force.py:mode_of

chunk_findings.detail: The bug states `[merge]` is not registered on `Config`, so `require_gates` is unreachable. The patch only replaces the `getattr` fallback with `cfg.merge.require_gates` and does not register the section. On a real config object with no `merge` attribute (the state the bug describes), `mode_of` raises `AttributeError` before any gate decision, so every merge that calls `assess` dies instead of warning. The new ratchet test only greps the source for the name, so it stays green while the knob is still not consumed at runtime. Example: `mode_of(Config())` where `Config` has no `merge` field.
